claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical-heterostructured state characterized by multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Rapid in-situ nanoscale mechanical testing can be performed concurrently with high-resolution imaging of evolving microstructures.
The proposed imaging can capture defect formation and grain-boundary dynamics during mechanical loading.
Real-time mechanical and microstructural measurements can be used as inputs to a machine-learning model calibrated against known mechanical responses.
Chemical fluctuations, grain-boundary characteristics, and defect populations evolve during mechanical loading and constitute predictive structural mediators.
Correlations between dynamic microstructural signatures and stress-deformation data enable prediction of bulk mechanical properties.
Using measured structure-property correlations bypasses the need for extensive a priori simulations.
The integrated method will predict Young's modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The integrated method will predict yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The integrated method will predict toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Prediction errors for Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness will be within 15%.
The proposed method will provide up to a fivefold improvement in time and computational efficiency over current CALPHAD, first-principles, and machine-learning methods.
Prior thermophysical-parameter, CALPHAD, first-principles, and conventional machine-learning methods are computationally intensive.
Prior methods have prediction errors of approximately 20–30% for the relevant mechanical properties.
The method may become unreliable when imaging resolution is insufficient to capture critical microstructural changes.
The method may become unreliable when signal noise obscures predictive microstructural indicators.
The method may become unreliable when the material's heterostructural state or testing environment lies substantially outside the model's calibration regime.
Extensive high-throughput in-situ datasets for complex heterostructured alloys are currently lacking.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if at least 80% of tested samples have an average absolute prediction error exceeding 15%.
